PullRequest.Title: Add Rust workspace workload tags
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- detect Rust workspaces from root `Cargo.toml` manifests
- report allowlisted direct Cargo dependency tags across normal, workspace, dev, build, target-specific, table, dotted, and renamed dependency declarations
- add aggregate and per-crate telemetry classifications, including Azure SDK for Rust crates
- add focused Cargo manifest parser coverage

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\tags\test\node\workspaceTags.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- hygiene check on all changed files

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Rust single-folder or multi-root workspace with usage telemetry enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: LifecyclePhase.Eventually constructs WorkspaceTags and starts getTags; workspace-tag telemetry waits for tag collection, but editor/workbench progress does not wait for it, so the Cargo work is off the user startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists call and at most one read per tag collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes workspace root inspection and telemetry emission, but is off the workbench startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve immediate children for every workspace root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolveAll batch containing R workspace roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same root directory batch was already performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before root manifest names, including Cargo.toml, are known and before workspace-tag telemetry can emit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe Cargo.toml existence in each workspace root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: When any resolved root contains Cargo.toml, R exists calls are issued, where R is the workspace-root count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All probes must settle before workspace-tag telemetry emits; they do not block editor/workbench readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each root Cargo.toml that exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: C reads, where C is the number of workspace roots with a root Cargo.toml; one read in the usual single-root Rust workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cargo.toml was not read by workspace-tag collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each read and synchronous parse must finish before workspace-tag telemetry emits; this remains off the workbench startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe/read existing package, Python, Maven, Gradle, Go, and Android marker files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-root probes and reads based on aggregated root names, plus one Android existence probe per root.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These probes and reads already ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs concurrently with Cargo probes in the same Promise.all and already gated workspace-tag telemetry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and enqueue the workspce.tags telemetry event
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event per contribution run; Cargo adds only allowlisted boolean fields, bounded by the fixed crate list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The event already existed; its payload lacked Cargo fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after tag collection and is not awaited by workbench startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with R workspace roots for existence probes, C root Cargo manifests for reads, and total Cargo.toml lines/dependency declarations for linear parsing. Effective cardinality is normally R=1 and C=1; the fixed allowlist bounds emitted Cargo fields.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All root Cargo existence probes and reads are joined into the existing Promise.all with other manifest probes, without a separate limiter. The overall tag result is cached after the first completed getTags call, so this does not recur during the session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold session performs tag collection once. After resolveWorkspaceTags completes, WorkspaceTagsService._tags serves warm getTags calls without more Cargo I/O or parsing. No cross-session cache is used, consistent with workspace telemetry collection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call path, exact R-probe/C-read multiplicity, Promise.all concurrency, linear parser, one-session cache, and eventual lifecycle placement are directly established by the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote filesystem latency and unusually large multi-root counts can increase background I/O, but typical root Cargo manifests and root counts are small; no evidence shows this eventual telemetry work causes user-visible contention or latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff introduces bounded, once-per-session Cargo manifest I/O and linear parsing for the requested telemetry. Although probes fan out by workspace root, the realistic cardinality is small and the work is off the user startup critical path, so the evidence does not establish an actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a workspace with no root Cargo.toml while usage telemetry is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing root-directory resolveAll completes, the lowercase name set shows no cargo.toml, getFilePromises returns an empty array, and workspace-tag telemetry proceeds without Cargo manifest work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve immediate children for all workspace roots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing resolveAll batch containing R roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates workspace-tag telemetry only; it is off workbench readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero exists calls and zero reads because nameSet lacks cargo.toml.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Cargo operation existed; changed behavior also performs none in this scenario.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Only the existing R-root directory listing scales; the Cargo-specific effective cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No Cargo promises are created. Existing workspace-tag probes retain their prior concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resulting non-Rust tags are cached for the session after the first collection; no negative Cargo cache beyond the whole-result cache is needed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: getFilePromises immediately returns [] when the aggregated lowercase name set lacks cargo.toml.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism: the guard deterministically avoids Cargo filesystem and parser work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Non-Rust workspaces incur only a constant tag assignment/import overhead and no new Cargo boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. Traced eventual workspace telemetry, one-session caching, root enumeration, Cargo filesystem fan-out, parser allocation/CPU scaling, Promise.all concurrency, and telemetry serialization. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
